thread:
Lydia Chen: heads-up — customer acme-health reported a big drop in embeddings vectors/sec starting ~2026-03-14 21:00 UTC. tokens/sec for their text generation calls looks stable, but embeddings rate is ~10x lower. they say latency spiked and some requests returned 500 'internal: dimension mismatch' intermittently. attaching summary below.

Omar Patel: noted. link to customer convo? any sample payloads and model?

Lydia Chen: they use model `embed-512-v1` (public catalog). sample payload from customer: 
```json
{
  "model": "embed-512-v1",
  "input": ["short sentence 1", "another sentence"],
  "batching": true
}
```
Errors from server: occasionally `Error: dimension mismatch: expected 512 got 768` in application logs, but most calls just slow / queue. we observed 500/502 spikes around 21:03. reported vectors/sec dropped from ~1200 to ~95.

Rachel Kim: thanks @Lydia — do we have queues/metrics from runtime for that time window (batcher queue depth, avg batch size, GPU util)?

Lydia Chen: pasted recent metrics snippet: 
```
time=2026-03-14T21:04:12Z queue_depth=46 avg_batch_size=2.1 batch_latency_ms=460 gpu_mem_pct=94 gpu_util_pct=18 kv_cache_hits=0
```
Interestingly GPU utilization is low while memory is high. looks like many small batches are being flushed slowly.

Ben Saito: low compute util + high mem usually means lots of loading / context or stalled workers. could be KV cache thrash or a blocking I/O op in the model loader. did the customer pin a new model variant or switch quantization?

Lydia Chen: they said they flipped to `embed-512-high-precision` yesterday but then tried revert. suspect config churn. also saw some 403s earlier in their timeline (auth tokens rotated) — support-bot flagged them but they re-auth'd. not sure if those 403s caused retries and queue bloat.

Omar Patel: can reproduce-ish on a repro account. I ran a synthetic load targeting embed endpoint with similar payloads:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-512-v1","input":["s1","s2","s3","s4"],"max_tokens":1}'; done
```
Observed avg vectors/sec ~80 and queue_depth climbed to 40 within 90s. CPU bound on the host managing batching.

Rachel Kim: can you grab an example request trace (x-request-id) where we saw dimension mismatch? need full headers + payload + backend route. also check runtime config changes around 20:45-21:10 (deploy, runtime flags).

Lydia Chen: x-req-id 9f2b6a7b attached from customer. payload same as above. server log excerpt: 
```
[21:03:05] session=9f2b6a7b route=/embeddings worker=aws-gpu-34 batch_size=1 Error: dimension mismatch (expected 512 got 768)
[21:03:06] session=9f2b6a7b batcher enqueue -> queue_depth=41
[21:03:07] session=... worker mem load 93%
```
Some sessions show mismatch, others succeed.

Ben Saito: that suggests mixed model variants serving the same route. if routing policy allows fallback between `embed-512-v1` and a 768-dim model, client will see inconsistent dims. check the model catalog mapping and either pin customer to explicit model id or enforce response shape validation.

Omar Patel: checked routing policy — there was a rollout yesterday: `embed-512-v1` -> 512 quantized variant and a canary with a 768 backbone mistakenly added to the same family. rollout record: 
```
- 2026-03-14T20:30 deploy canary model embed-768-exp -> route: /embeddings (tags: cheap-high-recall)
- 2026-03-14T20:55 rollback partial but route mapping not removed for dedicated customers
```
I'll open a kill-switch to stop routing to embed-768-exp for now.

Rachel Kim: good catch. that explains dimension mismatch. still need to understand why vectors/sec dropped — mixed dims would cause rejects but not queue-depth driven slowdown. any change in batcher config?

Omar Patel: found a config flip at 20:58 in staging->prod sync: `batcher.max_batch_size` was lowered from 64 to 8 and `batcher.batch_timeout_ms` increased from 30 -> 250 to favor throughput for other workloads. that makes many small batches and increases latency for short inputs.

Lydia Chen: so combination of small max_batch_size + long timeout + routing churn caused a pile-up. customers had retries for 403, causing more concurrent requests.

Ben Saito: mitigation plan: 
1) kill canary routing to 768 model (Omar) :heavy_check_mark:
2) revert batcher.max_batch_size to 64 for embeddings route (Omar/infra)
3) temporarily set `batcher.backpressure_threshold` lower so we 429 fast instead of piling up (Rachel/infra)
4) ask customer to pin model id and re-run tests (Lydia)

Rachel Kim: also adding a quick health-check that checks response vector dimension and logs a metric `embed_response_dim_mismatch_count` so we can alert earlier. I'll create a small rollout.

Lydia Chen: repro steps for customer-facing validation: 
1) pin model by id in payload: "model_id": "embed-512-v1-20260201"
2) run parallel clients 50x and measure vectors/sec and 95p latency
3) if you still see dim mismatch, include `x-request-id` header in report

Omar Patel: I've disabled routing to embed-768-exp and reverted batcher.max_batch_size on the test cluster. early metrics: queue_depth dropped from 46 -> 6 within 2 minutes, avg_batch_size increased to 12, gpu_util rose to 46% and vectors/sec climbed back to ~1100.

support-bot: incident created: INC-2026-03-14-emb-vec-rate. assigned to eng-runtime.

Lydia Chen: told customer we rolled back routing and batcher config and asked them to re-run their load. I'll monitor and update. thanks team. :thumbsup:

Rachel Kim: follow-ups: (1) audit recent rollout scripts to ensure model ids vs family tags are strict (2) add unit test to prevent 768-dim model from joining 512 family (3) dashboard widget for queue_depth per route. I'll open PRs.

Ben Saito: we should also add a runtime guard: if avg_batch_size < 2 and queue_depth > 20 and gpu_util < 30 then auto-scale more workers or short-circuit 429. filing follow-up
